_comment: Golden wire fixtures for the generated command clients.
Every client that speaks the command surface must agree on these exact
bytes. The bytes were produced by protoc itself (protoc --encode), not by
any one client, so no language is the privileged definition of the wire
format - each is checked against a neutral third party.
Follows the pattern of spec/continuity/queue-hash-fixtures.json: one file,
read by every platform's test suite. A client that drifts fails here rather
than in production on the platform nobody was testing.
To add a case: write the message in protobuf text format and run

cases.name: artist-request
cases.why: Both fields are required. The old hand-written facade checked this at runtime with 'guard let remoteId, let serverId else { fail }'; here it is the shape of the message.

cases.name: albums-request-paged
cases.why: A cursor is opaque to clients - they hand back whatever the previous page gave them. This pins that it survives a round trip unaltered.

cases.name: failure-response
cases.why: Failure is a variant of the result, not a side channel, so a client cannot forget to handle it.

cases.name: library-changed-event
cases.why: Events are pushed from the core unprompted, for an active subscription. If this stops decoding, live updates break silently rather than loudly.
